title: Force and Newton's Laws of Motion

questions.prompt: What is a force?
questions.explain: Forces are pushes and pulls. They are needed to change how something moves.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explain: Force is measured in newtons, named after Isaac Newton.

questions.prompt: Every force has a size and a...
questions.explain: To describe a force, you need to know how strong it is and which way it pushes or pulls.

questions.prompt: What is net force?
questions.answer: The combination of all forces on an object
questions.explain: Net force is what you get when you add up all the forces, taking their directions into account.

questions.prompt: What is inertia?
questions.answer: An object's resistance to a change in motion
wrong: The pull of gravity on an object
A kind of friction on rough ground
How fast an object is moving
questions.explain: Objects tend to keep doing what they are doing, whether staying still or moving.

questions.prompt: Which scientist described the laws of motion, and has the unit of force named after him?
questions.explain: Isaac Newton described how forces change motion, so the unit of force is the newton.

questions.prompt: Newton's first law of motion is also called the law of...
questions.explain: The first law says objects resist changes in motion, which is what inertia means.

questions.prompt: A soccer ball sits still on the grass. According to Newton's first law, what will it do?
questions.answer: Stay still unless a force acts on it
questions.explain: An object at rest stays at rest until a net force, like a kick, acts on it.

questions.prompt: A ball rolling across grass slowly comes to a stop. Why?
questions.answer: Friction from the grass acts on it
questions.explain: A moving object keeps moving unless a force acts on it. Here, friction slows the ball down.

questions.prompt: Squeezing an empty can until it crumples shows that a force can...
questions.explain: Forces can start motion, change speed or direction, or change an object's shape.

questions.prompt: Two kids push a box the same way, one with 10 N and one with 15 N. What is the net force?
questions.explain: Forces in the same direction add up: 10 N + 15 N = 25 N.

questions.prompt: What is needed to change an object's speed or direction?
questions.explain: Without a net force, an object keeps the same speed and direction.

questions.prompt: Two teams pull a rope with equal force in opposite directions. What happens?
questions.answer: The rope doesn't move; the net force is zero
wrong: The rope moves toward the left team
The rope moves toward the right team
The rope speeds up in both directions
questions.explain: Equal forces in opposite directions cancel out, so they are balanced.

questions.prompt: About how much force does it take to hold up a small apple?
questions.explain: A newton is a small amount of force, about what a small apple weighs.

questions.prompt: You kick a ball in deep space, far from any planet or star. What happens to it?
questions.answer: It keeps moving at the same speed and direction
wrong: It slowly drifts to a stop
questions.explain: With no friction, air or nearby gravity, there is no force to change its motion.

questions.prompt: A box is pushed 30 N to the right and 12 N to the left. What is the net force?
questions.explain: Opposite forces subtract: 30 N - 12 N = 18 N, in the direction of the bigger force.

questions.prompt: Force = mass × acceleration. What force is needed to make a 5 kg cart accelerate at 2 m/s²?
questions.explain: F = m × a = 5 kg × 2 m/s² = 10 N.

questions.prompt: A 3 kg ball accelerates at 4 m/s² when pushed. How big was the force? (Force = mass × acceleration)
questions.explain: F = m × a = 3 kg × 4 m/s² = 12 N.

questions.prompt: A net force of 10 N pushes a 2 kg box. What is its acceleration? (Acceleration = force ÷ mass)
questions.explain: a = F ÷ m = 10 N ÷ 2 kg = 5 m/s².

questions.prompt: A bus stops suddenly and the passengers lurch forward. Why?
questions.answer: Their bodies tend to keep moving forward
questions.explain: Because of inertia, the passengers keep moving even though the bus has stopped.

questions.prompt: Which is harder to start moving: an empty shopping cart or a full one?
questions.answer: The full cart, because it has more mass
wrong: The empty cart, because it has less mass
questions.explain: More mass means more inertia, so it takes more force to change its motion.

questions.prompt: A hockey puck glides across smooth ice in a straight line at a steady speed. What is the net force on it?
questions.explain: If speed and direction aren't changing, the forces are balanced, so the net force is about zero.
